statement: The median of a list of numbers is the middle value once the list is sorted. If the list has an even length there is no single middle value, and the median is the mean of the two middle values.

The numbers in nums arrive one at a time, in order. Keep track of them so that the median can be read at any moment, and return the median of all of them once the last one has arrived, as a decimal number.

The usual structure uses two heaps: a max-heap holding the smaller half of the numbers and a min-heap holding the larger half, balanced so that their sizes differ by at most one. The median then depends only on the two roots.

examples.explanation: Sorted, the numbers are 1, 3, 5, 15. The two middle values are 3 and 5, so the median is (3 + 5) / 2 = 4.0. The two heaps end up as {1, 3} and {5, 15}.
Every number is 2, so both middle values are 2 and the median is 2.0.
With an odd count there is one middle value: the median of 1, 2, 3 is 2.0.
